title: Hourly to Annual: Your Australian Pay Guide and the Average Salary Japan Context
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual salary using the 38-hour week formula. Includes tax, super, casual loading, and a note on average salary Japan for comparison.
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week, your annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour gives $1,004.90 per week or $52,254.80 per year.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For full-time employees, we assume 38 hours per week. So annual = hourly × 38 × 52. For part-time or casual, use your usual weekly hours. Our calculator on [the timesheet](/) does this for you.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. From 1 July 2026, the casual minimum rate is $33.05 per hour (base $26.44 plus 25% loading). Our calculator has a checkbox to add casual loading on top of your base rate – never enter a rate that already includes loading.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated and is it included in my salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% of your gross pay, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. It is not deducted from your salary; it is an additional benefit. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more details.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Conversion

When you know your hourly rate, working out your annual salary is straightforward. The basic formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Commission. This gives you a consistent annual figure to compare against job offers or to estimate your tax and super.

### Why 38 Hours?

The National Minimum Wage and most modern awards define full-time work as 38 ordinary hours per week. The Fair Work Ombudsman and Fair Work Commission both use this benchmark. If you work different hours – for example, 40 hours – you can adjust the formula accordingly. Our calculator on [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your own weekly hours.

### The Fortnightly View

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour:
- Weekly: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.90
- Fortnightly: $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80

Knowing your fortnightly amount helps with budgeting and matches common pay cycles.

## Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

Australia has several minimum pay rates depending on your employment type.

### National Minimum Wage

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This applies to award/agreement-free employees aged 21 or over. Juniors, apprentices, and employees with a disability have special rates, as detailed in the National Minimum Wage Order 2026.

### Award Rates

Most employees are covered by a modern award. Award minimum wages increased by 4.75% from 1 July 2026. Each award has its own classification rates, allowances, and penalty rates. You can find the right pay guide on our [pay guides](/blog) page.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (annual leave, sick leave). The casual minimum rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 + 25%). Our calculator includes a checkbox to add casual loading – never enter a rate that already includes loading.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation is an employer contribution of 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. It is not deducted from your gross pay. The super guarantee applies up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, on a $70,000 annual salary, your employer would contribute $8,400 in super. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more.

## Tax and Medicare Levy

Your annual gross pay is used to calculate income tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:
- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 + 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 + 37% on excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,420 + 45% on excess over $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. Single reduction thresholds (for low-income earners) are based on 2025–26 figures as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of calculation. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool estimates your net income after tax and Medicare.

### Example: National Minimum Wage

- Hourly rate: $26.44
- Weekly (38h): $1,004.90
- Annual gross: $52,254.80
- Estimated tax (2026–27): $5,108 (using full tax-free threshold)
- Medicare levy: $1,045
- Net annual: $46,101
- Super (12%): $6,270.58 on top

## A Note on Average Salary Japan

You may be curious about how Australian pay compares internationally, such as the average salary Japan. While we don't provide average salary Japan figures here, our focus is on converting your Australian hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and after-tax amounts. If you are researching average salary Japan, we recommend consulting official Japanese statistics or the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) data. Our calculator helps you understand your own pay in the Australian context.

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For precise pay rates, always check the relevant award or agreement. Use our [reference tables](/data) for historical rates and our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page for more examples.
